question: Should OpenClaw accept the experimental Claw lifecycle ownership model as a permanent core Doctor surface after its prerequisite ownership contract lands?
rationale: This is a new core lifecycle and persisted-state diagnostic capability on top of an open RFC stack; the experiment gate and implementation tests do not establish the long-term ownership or support boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded core diagnostics surface
options.body: Accept the direction only after the prerequisite lands, the live-database read is made concurrency-safe, and real current-head proof is attached.

options.title: Defer the whole Claws stack
options.body: Keep this PR and its dependents unlanded until maintainers evaluate the lifecycle model as one product decision.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Reject the proposed core lifecycle model if its functionality should remain outside OpenClaw's core architecture.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded core diagnostics surface
recommendation.body: Accept the direction only after the prerequisite lands, the live-database read is made concurrency-safe, and real current-head proof is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared-state and Doctor architecture work provides the closest evidence-backed ownership connection for this product and state-safety decision.
